slides.0.title: The wine service sequence
slides.0.subtitle: Smooth, quiet and centred on the guest
slides.1.title: From order to opening
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Presenting the bottle
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Show the label to the host and confirm producer, wine and vintage; if the vintage or wine differs from the list, say so before opening
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Cutting the foil and opening
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Cut the foil below the lip and wipe the neck; open quietly without shaking the bottle, and the cork can be placed on a small plate for the host to inspect
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Tasting and pouring
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Pour a small taste for the host to check for faults (such as cork taint), then serve the guests in order, the host last; do not overfill, leaving room for aroma
slides.1.content: Every step of service is a check: the wine, its quality and the guest’s pace.
slides.2.title: Sparkling wine and special cases
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Opening sparkling wine safely
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Chill the wine thoroughly; keep a thumb on the cork while loosening the cage, hold the bottle at about 45 degrees pointing away from people, and turn the bottle, not the cork, so the gas escapes with a gentle sigh
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Handling a faulty bottle
slides.2.highlights.1.content: If the host or sommelier judges the wine faulty (e.g. TCA), politely replace it with a fresh bottle of the same wine; do not argue with the guest, and offer an alternative if needed
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Recommending and communicating
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Ask about budget, preferences and dishes first, then offer two or three options at different prices with reasons, in language the guest understands rather than recited jargon
slides.2.content: Good wine service makes guests feel cared for, not examined.

C. The length of the cork

C. Decant it to hide the fault
D. Politely replace it with a fresh bottle
